interface.title: ProteinScope
interface.stage_of_work: Background research and target triage before experimental or computational work
interface.what_it_is_for: Type one protein identifier (gene symbol, UniProt accession or PDB code) and get a single dashboard that pulls together UniProt function and curation status, ranked PDB structures with a 3D viewer, the STRING interaction network, InterPro domains, Reactome pathways, CATH/SCOP classification, subcellular localization, diseases, references and the sequence with FASTA export.

data.note: No files were uploaded. All data came live from public services (UniProt, STRING, InterPro, Reactome, RCSB PDB, PDBe SIFTS, PubMed) for the example chips TP53, APP, Q6L8H1 and ACTB, and for typed queries: 1tup, insulin (picked INSR, P06213), egfr (picked fruit-fly Egfr, P04412) and the nonsense string zzzqqq123. Downloads saved: P04637_TP53.fasta (454 bytes, correct header and sequence) and 1AIE.pdb (54 KB, real PDB file). The first TP53 load showed no structures (PDB Structures '—', no 3D panel, screens/008.webp). Querying 1tup straight after brought up 12 structures and the classification panel (screens/023.webp), so the first miss was most likely a temporary failure of the structure lookup.

features.name: Identifier resolver with disambiguation picker
features.general: One search box that accepts several kinds of ID. Exact database identifiers go straight to a record; free-text queries go to a candidate list that may not contain the intended record.
features.specific: Type a UniProt accession or PDB code, or click an example chip, and press QUERY or Enter to load the dashboard directly. Any other query longer than 2 characters runs a protein-name/full-text search, and if more than one hit comes back it shows '// N PROTEINS FOUND — SELECT ONE' cards (name, gene, accession, Swiss-Prot badge, organism). Exact gene-symbol lookup runs only when that search finds nothing, so most gene symbols land in the picker, and the canonical protein can be missing from it (no human EGFR for 'egfr', no TP53 for 'tp53'). An unknown ID shows an error banner.
steps: type a UniProt accession or PDB code, or click an example chip (the reliable routes)
press QUERY or Enter
if a picker appears, check that the intended organism and protein are among the cards and click it
if the intended protein is missing, re-query by its accession
the dashboard loads in stages, with progress messages
if nothing matches, read the error banner and change the query
serves_tasks: Look up an entry from an identifier and check its basic facts
Pick the intended entry from a list of candidate matches
Get clear feedback when nothing matches

features.name: Resolution-ranked structure list with 3D molecular viewer
features.general: A list of experimental models filtered and sorted by quality, linked to an interactive 3D view. Choosing an item loads it, and you can switch rendering style, rotate, zoom, reset and download the file.
features.specific: 'Structures (N)' list (PDB ID, method, resolution) next to the 3D Structure Viewer. Per the code, only the first 40 PDB cross-references are considered, entries are filtered (X-ray ≤3.5 Å, cryo-EM ≤4 Å, NMR kept), sorted by resolution alone and capped at 12, so a well-known entry such as 1TUP can be absent and top entries can be complexes where the query is a short peptide. Clicking a row loads it from RCSB with a chain colour legend. The View buttons are Cartoon, Surface (electrostatic, with a charge legend), Ball+Stick, Licorice and Spacefill; the highlighted button can fall out of sync after a new protein loads. Drag rotates, the wheel zooms, ⟳ Reset re-fits, and '↓ PDB' downloads the coordinates.
steps: click a PDB entry in the ranked list
wait for 'Loading <ID>…' to finish and read the chain legend to see which chains the entry contains
pick a representation (Cartoon, Surface, Ball+Stick, Licorice or Spacefill)
drag to rotate and scroll to zoom; hover shows atom labels
press Reset to re-fit
press ↓ PDB to save the file, or click another entry to compare
serves_tasks: Choose an experimental structure and inspect it in different renderings and orientations
Compare another structure of the same protein
Save the coordinates for other software

features.name: Evidence-coloured interaction star network
features.general: A network diagram centred on the item being studied. Edges are coloured by evidence type, and you can zoom, reset the layout, read scores and click through to the source.
features.specific: STRING Interaction Network: the query protein in the middle with 18 partners. Each node shows its combined score. Coloured edge strands stand for neighborhood, fusion, co-occurrence, co-expression, experimental, database and text-mining evidence, and grey dashed lines join partners to each other. The + / − / ⌂ buttons and the wheel zoom. Clicking a partner opens STRING. Flaky: the hover tooltip appeared in the first run (screens/011.webp) but not in the replay; dragged nodes drift back because the force layout keeps running, which also makes node clicks miss.
steps: read the hub-and-spoke layout and the evidence colour legend
read each partner's combined score on its node (hover tooltip is unreliable)
zoom with + / − / wheel to untangle the layout
press ⌂ to reset the layout
click a partner, once the layout has settled, to open it in STRING
serves_tasks: Find binding partners and how they connect to each other, rearranging the view as needed
Open a partner in the source database

features.name: Section-link navigation over a summary dashboard
features.general: A summary card with headline counts and links to each section. Clicking a link scrolls to that panel; links are usually, but not always, hidden for sections without data.
features.specific: The header card shows the accession, name, gene, organism, Swiss-Prot badge, keywords and outbound links (UniProt, STRING, InterPro, PDB(n)). A row of counts follows (amino acids, mass, STRING partners, InterPro entries, Reactome pathways, PDB structures). Section links (3D Structure, Interactions, Domains, Pathways, Localisation, Diseases, Sequence) scroll to each panel. Some are left out when there is no data (Q6L8H1 has no 3D Structure or Diseases link, screens/061.webp), but the replay saw a Diseases link over an empty Diseases panel for Q12888, so a link does not guarantee content.
steps: read the identity card and the curation badge
check the count row to see which data exist
click a section link to jump to that panel, and confirm the panel actually has content
serves_tasks: Look up an entry from an identifier and check its basic facts
Check which pathways the protein belongs to
Review where the protein sits in the cell and which diseases involve it

features.name: Numbered sequence block with FASTA export
features.general: Show a biological sequence in numbered blocks and export it in a standard format with a header that names the record.
features.specific: Protein Sequence panel (length and mass), 60 residues per line in groups of 10 with position numbers. '↓ Download FASTA' saves <accession>_<gene>.fasta with the header '>P04637|TP53|Cellular tumor antigen p53 [Homo sapiens]'.
steps: go to the Sequence section
read the numbered residues
press ↓ Download FASTA

features.name: Function summary with numbered literature citations
features.general: A curated description of what the item does, with numbered inline citations resolved to a formatted reference list that links to the source papers.
features.specific: The header card shows UniProt function text with bracketed citation numbers and a numbered reference list built from PubMed metadata (NCBI eUtils, IEEE style per the code), each with a PMID link.
steps: read the function text in the header card
match each bracketed number to the numbered reference list
click a PMID link to open the paper in PubMed
serves_tasks: Read the function summary and the literature it cites

features.name: Structure-derived fold classification cards
features.general: Fold classifications looked up for the top experimental structures and shown as cards, one per classified domain, naming the source structure.
features.specific: Structural Classification panel ('CATH · SCOP — via PDBe SIFTS · based on first 5 structures'): CATH cards show the class › architecture › topology path and SCOP cards the fold name, each with its source PDB ID. Classification is fetched per PDB entry without chain filtering, so cards from complexes can describe partner chains (RPA70 on 2B3G, Sir2 on 1YC5 for TP53). Classification IDs show '—' and the links point at bare base URLs.
steps: scroll to the Structural Classification panel
read each CATH and SCOP card and note its source PDB entry
check in the structure viewer whether that entry's classified chain is the query protein or a partner

screens_never_reached: Cryo-EM or NMR structures in the structure list: every protein tried (TP53, APP, INSR, ACTB, fly Egfr) listed only X-ray entries, so the method labels for other techniques were never seen

The STRING, UniProt, InterPro, Reactome, CATH, SCOP and PubMed pages behind the outbound links, citation PMIDs and partner-node clicks: they are external sites and do not load in this sandbox (clicking IGF1R opened a tab that could not load)
not_done: Did not run the BRCA1 or EGFR example chips; EGFR was tried only by typing 'egfr', which gave the picker

Typing 'egfr' gave a picker without human EGFR (P00533), only fly and bee Egfr, VOPP1 orthologs and CLEC14A (screens/065.webp). Per the review of index.html:294-311, the picker searches protein names and full text rather than gene symbols, so case is not the cause; the replay saw the same with 'tp53' (TP53 absent). Getting the human protein needs the chip or the accession.
The first TP53 load showed no PDB structures and no 3D or classification panels (screens/008.webp). Re-querying with 1tup fixed it (screens/023.webp), so it looked like a temporary failure.

In the 3D viewer, the highlighted View button can fall out of sync after a new protein loads. For INSR, Cartoon and Spacefill were both highlighted (screens/052.webp). For fly Egfr, Cartoon was highlighted while the model drew as a surface and off-centre (screens/073.webp, screens/074.webp) until Cartoon was pressed again (screens/075.webp).
The chain legend for 3I2T listed chains A–F but the cartoon looked a single colour (screens/075.webp). I did not check whether the other chains are drawn.
Associated Diseases cards show only description text, with a blank title line where the disease name should be (screens/018.webp)
The CATH/SCOP cards show '—' where the classification IDs should be, and their links point at bare base URLs (screens/038.webp)

InterPro entries are shown only as IDs and type tags, with no names or residue ranges, and there is no domain-position diagram to try. In the replay the count card said 20 InterPro entries for Q12888 while the panel listed about 14.

Node dragging in the network only partly held, because the layout pulls nodes back (screens/014.webp). Hovering an edge showed no tooltip (screens/016.webp). The node hover tooltip worked here (screens/011.webp) but not in the replay.

Why 1TUP is not in the top-12 list: per the review of index.html:548 and 581, only the first 40 PDB cross-references are ranked and 12 are kept, so 1TUP can fall outside. How the 'first 5 structures' used for CATH/SCOP are chosen was not checked.

Using the header's outbound links (UniProt, InterPro, PDB(n)) to check source records was never tried; it needs a run with external access before it can become a task.
Whether the viewer or the chain legend names which chain is the query protein (for example in 1YC5) was not inspected; it needs a new run before t4 can say how to tell the query chain apart.
